page.title: Capstan | Built for a friend with CMT
page.metaDescription: An Apple Vision Pro hardware engineer built a grip glove for his friend with CMT. A dial at the wrist closes your hand and holds it closed. No motor, no battery, no surgery.
page.eyebrow: From a founding engineer of Apple Vision Pro
page.h1: He built this glove so his friend could grip again.
page.lead: Our founder spent years building hardware at Apple. Then Mushruf, his close friend, started dropping cups. Mushruf has CMT, and he was told there was nothing for his hands. So we built Capstan. It is a thin glove with a dial at the wrist. The dial closes your hand and holds it closed. No motor, no battery, no surgery.
page.heroProof: First production run: 500 gloves. Founding members lock in $349.

problemBody: Dropping things. Jars and lids. Buttons and fly zips. Signing your name. Coins and keys.
Mushruf tried splints and task tools. They held his hand still or helped with one job at a time. You may have heard the same words he heard: there is nothing for your hands.
page.whyHead: Why an engineer, not a brace maker.
whyBody: Researchers asked 937 people with CMT what bothers them most. The top answer was weak hands and fingers. It came in above trouble walking.
Every device so far holds the hand in place or protects it. We treated grip as a hardware problem instead. Add strength from the outside. Hold it as long as it is needed. Keep the glove thin.

whyStats.small: people with CMT wear a leg or ankle brace
have anything at all for their hands

steps.head: Put it on
steps.body: Capstan is a thin glove. It slides on and straps at the wrist, like a bike glove.

steps.head: Turn the dial
steps.body: The dial at your wrist pulls the cables and closes your hand. Press the dial against a table if that is easier. One hand is enough.

steps.head: Grip, and rest
steps.body: The glove holds your grip so your muscles do not have to. It works like a seatbelt: click, hold, let go when you choose. No motor, no battery, nothing to charge.

page.proofHead: What we can show so far
page.proofStory: Mushruf, a close friend of our founder, was the first person to wear Capstan. He has CMT, and he got his glove free. He wore it every day for six weeks. With the glove on, he opened door handles again on the first try. His result is his own. Results vary from hand to hand.
page.proofLab: We also measured his grip in our lab. With the glove on, he could squeeze about four times harder than with his hand alone. That is one person, on one day. It is not a promise.
page.proofCreds: Capstan comes from engineers who built hardware at Apple. The design won a Red Dot Award in 2026. A patent is filed.
page.offerHead: One glove. One price. You own it.
offerBullets: Nothing to charge. Nothing to replace.

faq.q: Does it fit the left hand or the right hand?
faq.a: Both. We make left and right gloves, and you can wear one on each hand. When we fit you, we start with the hand you use most.
Each glove is fit to your hand. After you sign up, we send a short guide with three simple measurements to take. It takes a few minutes with a tape measure.

faq.q: Will it work for my type of CMT?
faq.a: Capstan works from the outside of your hand. It closes your fingers and holds them closed. It does not depend on your CMT type. What matters is fit, and we check fit with you before your glove ships.

faq.q: I have arthritis or a stroke, not CMT. Can I use it?
faq.a: Our first run is for people with CMT, so we can do one thing well. Join the list and tell us about your hands. We will email you when Capstan is ready for more conditions.

faq.q: Can I put it on with one hand?
faq.a: Capstan is built for one-handed use, and we check this with you at your fitting. After you sign up, a short survey asks which hand you use. That way we check the fit that matters most for you.

faq.q: What if it does not work for me?
faq.a: Send it back within 30 days for a full refund. One email is all it takes.
The first run of 500 gloves ships this fall. People on the list order first, in the order they joined.

faq.q: Can I pay with an HSA or FSA card?
faq.a: We do not know yet. We will email the list the moment we know.

faq.q: I am researching this for a parent. What should I do?
faq.a: Join the list for them. We will send a printable one-page guide you can hand to them, written in plain words.

page.finalHead: Save your spot in the first 500.
page.scopeLine: Capstan is a mechanical grip aid. It does not treat or slow CMT.
